subject: POC/Trial: Environment setup and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: POC/Trial: Environment setup and success criteria

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed plan for the POC/trial so your team can evaluate Redwood across functionality, latency/cost, and security.

Summary / success criteria (please confirm):
- Quality: model responses meet your user-facing thresholds on intent accuracy and hallucination rate (target: >= 92% intent accuracy on the eval set).
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 400ms on the typical prompt mix.
- Throughput: achieve sustained 10 req/s per model variant during peak simulation.
- Cost: token cost and throughput profile documented, with recommendations to reach target unit economics.
- Security/compliance: ability to run in a VPC or Private deployment and confirm data handling/retention meets Acme policies.

Evaluation plan / timeline (proposal):
1) Week 0 (prep) — share sample prompts, 500-1k eval examples, and small dataset subset. Acme provides allowlist IPs and primary contact.
2) Week 1 (hosted sandbox) — quick smoke and UX: 1-2 days setup on our hosted trial environment. Validate quality & basic latency.
3) Week 2 (dedicated sandbox) — reserved capacity for throughput and load tests (3-5 days).
4) Week 3+ (VPC/private) — if needed for compliance, we can provision a VPC trial (1-2 weeks depending on networking and KMS).

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (PM) / Connor (AE) / Dylan (SE) for setup and runbooks.
- Acme: Alex (product) / Sara (infra) for dataset, credentials, and approvals.

Immediate next steps:
- Confirm you want to start with Hosted -> Dedicated -> VPC or skip steps.
- Share sample prompts + eval set by EOD Fri (2026-02-27).
- Sign the attached POC SOW (poc_sow_v1.pdf) so we can reserve dedicated capacity.

Attachments: poc_sow_v1.pdf, redwood-trial-ops-checklist.xlsx

Happy to adjust — tagging Dylan for any SE-level constraints.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — thanks for the questions, answers below and a recommended path: Hosted -> Dedicated -> VPC (if required).

1) Logs & retention (hosted trial):
- For hosted sandbox trials logs are retained for 30 days by default; we can enable a shorter retention or opt-out of storing raw prompt text for trial accounts.
- We redact known PII by pattern and offer a configuration flag to disable request/response logging entirely for sensitive evaluations.
- For Dedicated and VPC trials, logs stay within the tenant's reserved environment; VPC + customer KMS allows you to control keys for any stored artifacts.

2) Dedicated sandbox noisy-neighbor guarantees:
- Dedicated capacity is provisioned as reserved GPU pools; for the sandbox we will reserve a small pool sized to your test profile. We provide an SLO for throughput during the POC window (details in attached SOW).
- Connor will coordinate sizing based on the eval prompts you send.

3) SOC 2: attaching a redwood_soc2_summary.pdf to this thread and linking our cert: https://redwood.example.com/soc2-cert

Recommended path & timelines (reiterated):
- Start with hosted sandbox (1-2 days) to validate prompt quality and get initial metrics.
- Move to dedicated sandbox (3-5 days) to run sustained throughput/cost experiments.
- If Acme requires network isolation and KMS control we schedule a VPC/private trial (1-2 weeks).

Action items for Acme: share eval prompts + small dataset, provide allowlist IPs, confirm kickoff week (you suggested 3/8).

Connor / Dylan — please see below and advise on sizing and any blockers for the dedicated sandbox.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: POC/Trial: Environment setup and success criteria — SE notes on VPC/deployment

Hi all — quick tech notes for Sara and Alex about what a VPC trial will need and what we can do during the hosted/dedicated phases: 

- Hosted sandbox: minimal network work — standard API key auth, TLS in transit, logs retained per Marissa's note. Good for early QA.
- Dedicated sandbox: we'll provision reserved GPU nodes in our tenant for the test. We need a list of expected peak concurrency and typical sequence lengths (tokens) to size correctly.
- VPC trial (customer-managed networking):
  * Allowlist our egress IPs (we'll provide ranges) or set up a private peering link.
  * Open outbound ports 443 (TLS) and 8443 (optional admin endpoints).
  * KMS integration: we support AWS KMS / GCP KMS customer-managed keys. Key rotation and access policies are required.
  * Audit logs: we can ship logs to your S3/GCS endpoint or forward to your SIEM — retention and format can be configured.

Minimum test config for the POC (recommended):
- 2x GPU nodes (g4dn-like) for functional test; 4x for throughput stress.
- Provide a 200-500 prompt eval set with expected p95 latency targets.

I'll attach a short network requirements file for Sara: vpc_network_requirements.txt. Happy to jump on a quick call with your infra team.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
